title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: The diameter is the length (in edges) of the longest path between any two nodes. The path may or may not pass through the root. Return the diameter.

hints.1_question: Think of the longest path as turning around at some 'top' node. What does the path length at that node depend on?
hints.2_nudge: At each node, the best path turning there is height(left) + height(right). Compute heights bottom-up and keep a global maximum.
hints.3_big_hint: h(n) returns 1 + max(h(left), h(right)); before returning, best = max(best, h(left) + h(right)).

known_bugs.name: only measures the path through the root
known_bugs.followup: Could the longest path avoid the root entirely, living inside one subtree?

known_bugs.name: counts nodes instead of edges
known_bugs.followup: How many edges does a single node have in any path?

known_bugs.name: takes max(left, right) instead of left + right
known_bugs.followup: A path that goes down the left side and down the right side uses both heights. Which of your two terms is missing?

followups: How would you return the endpoints of the diameter?
